proposedTopics.title: Stack
proposedTopics.description: LIFO structure for matching, undo/backtrack-style state, and deferred-processing patterns. Independent axis from Two Pointers, also array-based.

proposedTopics.title: Monotonic stack
proposedTopics.description: Keep the stack sorted (increasing or decreasing) by popping elements that violate the order before pushing; popped element's answer is resolved by the pusher. Recognize: "next greater/smaller element", "days until warmer".

proposedTopics.title: Valid parentheses / matching pairs
proposedTopics.description: Push openers, pop-and-check on closers; stack empty at the end means fully matched. Recognize: nested bracket/tag validity, "remove adjacent duplicates".

proposedTopics.title: Expression evaluation
proposedTopics.description: Use a stack to hold operands/partial results while scanning an expression left to right, applying operator precedence explicitly. Recognize: calculator problems, Reverse Polish Notation.

proposedTopics.title: Min-stack design
proposedTopics.description: Track the running minimum alongside each push (auxiliary stack or encoded value) so getMin is O(1). Recognize: "design a stack that also supports X in O(1)".

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a monotonic stack? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "next/previous greater or smaller element", "days until a warmer day", spans, or a histogram/skyline where each element's answer depends on the nearest bigger/smaller neighbor. Pitfall: choosing the wrong monotonic direction, or storing values when you need indices (distances/widths require indices) — and forgetting to drain the leftover stack at the end. Related: Online Stock Span is the same pop-while-smaller span count.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the next-greater-element scan in your language of choice: for each array position, find the next element to its right that is strictly greater (or a sentinel if none).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Stack holds indices of positions still waiting for their answer. For each i, while the stack's top element is smaller than nums[i], pop it and record i (or nums[i]) as its next-greater. Then push i. Invariant: the stack's values stay decreasing top-to-bottom; anything left at the end has no greater element.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Next Greater Element I (Easy) — for each value in nums1, find its next greater element in nums2 (elements of nums1 are a subset of nums2).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Monotonic stack over nums2 builds a value -> next-greater map in one pass; then look up each nums1 value.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Daily Temperatures (Medium) — for each day, how many days until a warmer temperature (0 if none).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Decreasing stack of indices; when today is warmer than the top, pop and the answer is i minus the popped index.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Largest Rectangle in Histogram (Hard) — largest rectangle area fitting under a bar-height histogram.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Increasing stack of indices; when a shorter bar arrives, pop and compute area = popped height times the width between the new left boundary and i. Use a trailing zero-height sentinel to flush the stack.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a push-openers / pop-on-closers stack? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: nested bracket/tag validity, balanced-symbol checks, "remove adjacent duplicates", or any structure where the most recently opened thing must close first (LIFO nesting). Pitfall: forgetting the two failure modes — a closer with an empty stack (or wrong opener on top) AND a non-empty stack at the end (unclosed openers). Related: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String pops when the top equals the incoming char.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the bracket matcher in your language of choice: scan a string of brackets and decide whether every closer matches the most recent unmatched opener.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Push each opener; on a closer, fail if the stack is empty or its top isn't the matching opener, else pop. Map each closer to its opener. Invariant: the stack always holds the still-open brackets in nesting order; valid means it ends empty.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Valid Parentheses (Easy) — return true if brackets '()[]{}' are correctly opened and closed in order.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Push openers, pop and match on closers; valid iff every close matches and the stack ends empty.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid (Medium) — fewest parentheses to insert so the string becomes valid.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Track open count; a ')' with no open to cancel adds one required insertion. Answer is leftover opens plus those unmatched closers (no actual stack needed, just a counter).

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Decode String (Medium) — expand encoded strings like "3[a2[c]]" into "accaccacc".
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Stack of partial results: on '[' push the current string and repeat count and reset; on ']' pop and repeat the built segment. The stack holds one frame per open bracket.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for a stack to evaluate an expression? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: calculator problems, Reverse Polish / postfix notation, expressions with operator precedence, or parentheses that defer evaluation. Pitfall: mishandling operator precedence and associativity — evaluate '*' and '/' immediately but defer '+' and '-', and watch operand order for non-commutative '-' and '/' (a op b, not b op a). Related: Basic Calculator (Hard) adds parentheses handling on the same stack idea.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write the RPN evaluator in your language of choice: evaluate a postfix expression given as a list of number and operator tokens.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Scan tokens; push numbers, and on an operator pop the top two operands (the second-popped is the left operand), apply, push the result. Invariant: after processing a valid expression the stack holds exactly one value — the answer.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation (Medium) — evaluate an arithmetic expression in postfix form.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Operand stack; pop two on each operator (mind order for '-' and '/'), push the result.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Basic Calculator II (Medium) — evaluate an infix string with + - * / and non-negative integers (no parentheses).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Keep a stack of pending additive terms; apply '*' and '/' immediately against the last pushed number, defer '+'/'-' by pushing (signed) values, then sum the stack.

proposedPrompts.promptText: When do you reach for the min-stack (running-extremum-per-entry) design? Name the problem-statement signals, and the classic pitfall.
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Signals: "design a stack that also returns the min/max in O(1)", any LIFO structure needing an auxiliary aggregate that must survive pops. Pitfall: storing only a single global min — it can't be restored after the min is popped; pair each entry with the min-so-far (aux stack or encoded pair) so pops roll it back. Related: Max Stack generalizes this with lazy deletion for arbitrary removal.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Write a min-stack in your language of choice: push, pop, top, and getMin all in O(1).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Alongside the value stack keep a second stack whose top is always the current minimum: on push, push min(value, current-min); on pop, pop both. Invariant: the min-stack's top mirrors the minimum of exactly the elements currently present.

proposedPrompts.promptText: Solve: Min Stack (Medium) — design a stack supporting push, pop, top, and getMin in O(1).
proposedPrompts.answerHint: Pair each pushed value with the min-so-far (aux stack or a tuple) so getMin reads the top and pops restore the previous min.
